clue.text: Medication provided when upset is a tonic

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the whole run of letters upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medication
provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'

explanation.surface: A patient who throws up their tablets hears that the medicine is a pick-me-up anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' turns PILL + IF over to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or stimulus, something that bucks you up like a tonic.

clue.text: Puts back a record player belonging to us, with note inside

parts.note: a DJ plays records

indicators.note: inside places the note within the word for belonging to us

parts.note: belonging to us means ours

explanation.surface: Someone postpones a meeting because a disc jockey of theirs has slipped a note in.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to postpone it, putting it back to a later time.

clue.text: Sea, we hear, reaches higher level, producing these?

definitions.text: Sea, we hear, reaches higher level, producing these?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word sea is taken by its sound, the letter C

parts.note: said aloud, sea is the name of the letter C
something that reaches a higher level rises

explanation.surface: A question about flooding: when sea levels rise, is this what follows?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rising seas are just the sort of thing that brings emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergencies or turning points, such as those caused when sea levels climb, are critical situations.

clue.text: Sign agreement with nothing but changes? Certainly

parts.note: nodding is a sign of agreement
O is the figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word but are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone nods along to anything except changes, apparently quite sure of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without question, an emphatic way of agreeing like certainly.

clue.text: Like speech uttered in halting way, as no word should be

definitions.text: Like speech uttered in halting way
definitions.meaning: faltering, imperfect speech, as in a halting attempt at a foreign tongue
a promise or pledge should never go unkept

explanation.definitionFit: Halting speech is described with this adjective, and a word that is not kept is described the same way.

clue.text: Once unit has regrouped, carry on

indicators.note: regrouped says the letters of once unit are rearranged into a new formation

explanation.surface: A military order: once the unit has got back together, keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going is to carry on, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Wrap for old female, affording protection in gale?

parts.note: to wind something is to wrap it round
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A shawl is offered to an elderly woman to keep her warm in stormy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that keeps out strong wind protects you in a gale, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Indication of direction to take from a river bank

parts.note: a bank of seats or switches is a row of them

explanation.surface: A signpost points the way to go when leaving a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer drawn on a sign shows which way to go, the standard indication of direction.

clue.text: Fool disturbed monarch who's modified form of entertainment

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters of fool are jumbled

parts.note: R is short for rex or regina, a monarch

indicators.note: modified says the letters of who's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jester unsettles a king who then changes his mind about the evening's amusements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges FOOL to FLOO; 'modified' rearranges WHOS to SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret staged in a nightclub is a kind of entertainment.

clue.text: Fish move across frozen lake, say

definitions.meaning: a flat fish of the ray family

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flat sea fish and also means to glide on blades over ice.

clue.text: Weapon originally featuring in Casebook of Sherlock Holmes

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A blunt instrument turns up in a collection of detective stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of Casebook of Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a short heavy club, a weapon used to strike someone.

clue.text: Son on piano in old-time musical performances

indicators.note: on puts the son after the rest, added on at the end
in places the piano's letter within the word for old-time

parts.note: O for old plus ERA for time
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A boy plays the piano at an old-fashioned variety show.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are staged dramas set to music, so they are musical performances.

clue.text: March past made him homesick

parts.note: not a parade but the end of the month: a Victorian poet abroad longed for England once April came

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning wrote 'Oh, to be in England now that April's there', homesick verse from Italy.

clue.text: Remote possibilities in houses accident damaged? (They're found in parts of other rows)

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of houses and accident are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An insurer weighs how unlikely it is that homes were wrecked by mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges HOUSES ACCIDENT. The bracket notes that the two words also turn up in pieces of other rows of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Long shots are unlikely possibilities, things with little hope of happening.

clue.text: Fearless university supporter mounted attack

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the word is set upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: a fan supports a team
a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: A college football fan launches a bold assault without fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Unafraid means without fear, a direct synonym of fearless.

clue.text: Guardian, for one, hasn't finished house in Dublin

indicators.note: hasn't finished drops the final letter of the newspaper word

parts.note: The Guardian is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: The newspaper has not completed its report on a building in the Irish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' removes the Y. The Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dail Eireann is the lower chamber of Ireland's parliament, which sits in Dublin.

clue.text: See 14
Counts, for example, as virtue

definitions.meaning: counts are titled aristocrats, members of the peerage
high moral worth and greatness of character

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers the titled class, earls and counts, and also loftiness of character.

clue.text: Labour anticipated providing incentive for this kind of union

definitions.text: Labour anticipated providing incentive for this kind of union

parts.words: Labour anticipated providing incentive for this kind of union
parts.note: not trade unions and politics: a baby on the way pushes a couple into a hasty marriage

explanation.definitionFit: A wedding forced on a couple because the bride is pregnant is called by this firearm name.

clue.text: Trout, say, that's good, if held back in a piece of net

indicators.note: in places the turned word within the a plus net piece

parts.note: mesh is a piece of netting

indicators.note: held back says the word if is turned round

explanation.surface: An angler is pleased if a trout is caught in the netting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' turns IF to FI, which goes 'in' A MESH.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout are caught by anglers for sport, an example of fish pursued as quarry.

clue.text: Tree doctor covering area brought in to preserve against decay

indicators.note: covering means the tree word goes round the other letters

parts.note: the elm is a tree
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon is called in to protect timber from rotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' just links: MB and A are what the tree covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Embalming treats a corpse to keep it from rotting, preserving it against decay.

clue.text: Religious teacher cut short by the Parisian mob

indicators.note: cut short drops the teacher word's last letter

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A rabbi is interrupted by a Paris crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the I from RABBI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble is a disorderly crowd, a mob.

clue.text: Ready to return English bishop imprisoned by judge

indicators.note: imprisoned by means the following word encloses the English bishop

parts.note: to rate is to judge or assess
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An English bishop jailed by a judge is ready to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is slang for cash, as in 'ready money', so 'Ready to return' is money handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is a partial refund, cash given back to the payer.

clue.text: Hospital's ending an examination — there's no news after that

indicators.note: ending picks out the final letter of the hospital word

parts.note: a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Hospital results come in and nothing more will be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent news is by definition the newest, with nothing following it.

clue.text: Examine small change in front of garment

indicators.note: in front of puts the coin's letter before the garment

parts.note: P, a penny, is small change
a robe is a garment

explanation.surface: Check whether there are coins in the pocket at the front of a dressing gown.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate closely, to examine.

clue.text: By a list it gets impaired?

definitions.text: By a list it gets impaired?

indicators.note: impaired says the letters of by a list it are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether drawing up a list damages steadiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets impaired' rearranges BY A LIST IT; the whole clue asks what is upset when the letters are.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiness or firmness is exactly what is lost when something is impaired.

clue.text: General holding large gun

indicators.note: holding means the general word wraps round the size letter

parts.note: rife means widespread, general

explanation.surface: An army general carries a big firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun.

clue.text: I must talk in order to save time, in a way

indicators.note: in order says the letters of I must talk are sorted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone insists on chatting so as not to waste a minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing several jobs at once is one way to save time.
